articles.title: A Gloucestershire gardener won £1.09 million on a Paddy Power game but received just £20,265; the High Court ordered the bookmaker to pay the remaining £1.07 million
articles.summary: A Gloucestershire gardener was told she had won more than £1 million on an online gambling game, only to receive a fraction of the displayed jackpot.
articles.body: A Gloucestershire gardener was told she had won more than £1 million on an online gambling game, only to receive a fraction of the displayed jackpot. Corrine Durber challenged Paddy Power’s decision to pay her just £20,265.14 after the company blamed a technical error. In March 2025, the High Court ruled in her favour, ordering the bookmaker to pay a further £1,076,867.57. The dispute began with a spin on an iPad in October 2020 and became a legal battle over whether a gambling company could refuse a prize shown on its own screen. The ruling raised important questions about digital game design, contractual terms and consumer protection. Here is how the jackpot appeared, why Paddy Power disputed it and what the judge decided.How the Wild Hatter game showed Corrine Durber a £1.1 million jackpot in 2020The dispute began on 18 October 2020, when Corrine Durber played the Wild Hatter game on her iPad through Paddy Power. According to The Guardian, the game combined the mechanics of a fruit machine with a wheel-of-fortune-style jackpot round. After progressing to the second stage and spinning the wheel, Durber’s screen indicated that she had won the “Monster Jackpot”, valued at £1,097,132.71.The apparent win looked like a life-changing result. Instead of receiving the full amount, Durber was paid a much smaller sum, setting off a legal fight that lasted more than four years before the High Court delivered its judgment in March 2025.Why Paddy Power paid £20,265.14 and blamed a software error for the jackpotPaddy Power paid Durber £20,265.14, saying she had won the smaller “Daily Jackpot” rather than the Monster Jackpot. The company argued that the game’s software had displayed the wrong result. The random number generator indicated that Durber had won the smaller prize, but an error in mapping the software caused the animation to show a different outcome.The distinction mattered because the amount displayed on the screen was more than £1 million higher than the sum she received. The BBC reported that the software-mapping error had affected 14 plays over a period of 48 days. Paddy Power maintained that the displayed jackpot did not reflect the result generated by the game’s underlying system.Durber challenged the decision rather than accepting the smaller payment. Her case centred on whether the company could rely on a technical fault to avoid paying a prize that its own game had presented as a win. The disagreement ultimately became a question of contract law: what was the customer entitled to expect when the game showed a specific jackpot?The High Court ordered Paddy Power to pay Corrine Durber £1,076,867.57Durber brought a claim against PPB Entertainment Limited, which operates Paddy Power, seeking the outstanding winnings on the basis that the displayed result formed part of the agreement between the player and the gambling company. On 5 March 2025, Mr Justice Ritchie granted judgment in her favour, ordering the company to pay £1,076,867.57.The amount represented the difference between the displayed jackpot of £1,097,132.71 and the £20,265.14 already paid. The judgment found that the discrepancy arose from human error in mapping the software, which had caused the animation to show the wrong result.The decision was significant because it rejected the idea that the company could simply disregard what the customer had seen on screen. It did not establish that every technical error automatically entitles a player to a displayed prize. Instead, the outcome depended on the particular game, its presentation and the contractual terms in the case.Justice Ritchie said ‘what you see is what you get’ was central to the gameIn his 62-page ruling, Justice Ritchie emphasised that players would reasonably expect the information displayed by a game to be accurate. He compared the situation with playing roulette in a physical casino. A customer who bets on number 13 expects the house to pay if the ball lands on that number. Similarly, a player using a digital game should be able to expect its displayed result to correspond with the outcome presented to them.The comparison helped explain why the software error did not automatically settle the question in Paddy Power’s favour. The company had relied on the random number generator, but the customer had been shown a different result by the game itself. The case therefore highlighted the importance of clear terms, accurate displays and adequate software testing in online gambling. It also demonstrated that technical explanations must be considered alongside the contractual expectations created by a product’s design.Corrine Durber celebrated her High Court victory as Paddy Power reviewed the judgmentFollowing the ruling, Durber said she was relieved and happy that the judge had confirmed she had won the jackpot fairly. She questioned why Paddy Power had not paid her immediately rather than putting her through a prolonged legal dispute. The case had taken years to resolve, and the difference between the amount displayed and the sum initially paid had left her fighting for the balance through the courts.The Guardian reported that Durber said she would never bet with Paddy Power again and advised others to be careful. The company expressed regret over the case and said it was reviewing the judgment. It also highlighted its wider record of paying customers’ winnings.The ruling established that the circumstances of an online game’s display can carry significant weight when a court assesses a customer’s contractual rights. For players, it underlined the importance of keeping records of disputed results. For operators, it offered a warning that software faults and the terms governing a game must be assessed carefully when a displayed outcome conflicts with the result generated behind the scenes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Turkiye moves to ratify Mecca defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: Trilateral deal between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan lays out provisions for joint defence.
articles.body:
The trilateral defence pact between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, has been submitted to the Turkish parliament for ratification.

The pact, signed on August 7, contains 16 articles, according to the document submitted to the Turkish parliament, seen by the Reuters news agency.

It aims to create a joint defence architecture in the region, in the case of an armed attack on any member, and lays out provisions in each article accordingly.

In Article 1 of the accord, for example, the signatories shall use “all necessary means” to eliminate threats to one another’s territorial integrity.

Once the first article is invoked, in case of an attack on any member state, the document lays out provisions for what follows next, as outlined in Article 2 of the draft seen by Reuters.

“In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the full range ‌of mutual assistance measures available to them,” says Article 2.

This point is similar to Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, NATO’s founding document, which treats an armed attack on one member as an attack on all.

Article 2 goes on to say that each signatory – Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye – “will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required”, adding that the three countries will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources.

Earlier this month, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under the mutual defence pact and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by Yemen’s Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God).

Articles 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the draft agreement, submitted to the Turkish parliament, also lay out details on defence industry cooperation, intelligence sharing, logistical support and joint training and the fight against “all means of terrorism”, including at the operational level.

Other provisions talk about joint research, development and innovation projects in the field of advanced technology and ensuring military readiness.

There is also mention of setting up a defence committee, which will include foreign and defence ministers from all three signatory states.

And there is a mechanism for allowing other states to join the agreement, with aspirants needing the approval of all three founding members.

The agreement will last 10 years, after which any country can withdraw according to the draft submitted to the Turkish parliament.

Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar speaking on the submitted pact said the process of ratification is going to take “quite some time”, despite the ruling coalition needing a simple majority.

“The various political parties that are represented in the Turkish parliament are going to discuss the provisions in the pact, and we could witness heated debates because the opposition has its own objectives,” he said.

Serdar said even if the deal is ratified, it would not lead to a deployment of Turkish troops, a move which will require other legislative processes.

Turkiye’s parliamentary speaker will refer the agreement to ⁠the parliament’s foreign affairs commission. The commission could debate the ⁠agreement as early as Friday, according to a source who spoke to Reuters.

Once it is submitted to the commission, the contents and details of the agreement are expected to be made public.

“This strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, and safeguard security and stability in our region,” Burhanettin Duran, the Turkish presidency’s communications director, said on X.

Duran added that the process marked an important milestone towards the “institutionalisation” of strategic cooperation between the three nations.

On Monday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke of the escalating violence between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.

“As I often say, we are surrounded by a ring of fire. That is exactly the situation we face,” Erdogan said, while referring to the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport.

In recent weeks, the Houthis have carried out missile and drone attacks against the kingdom, including oil facilities and Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government has launched air attacks on Houthi positions.

articles.body: JAMSHEDPUR: Odisha Police on Tuesday arrested a 40-year-old man from Jamshedpur in Jharkhand, nearly two months after he allegedly killed his mother and buried her body under the kitchen floor of their rented house in Puri, an official said.Police searched for the accused across Odisha and also visited Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu during the investigation, news agency PTI reported.The woman's body was recovered on August 24 after the house owner in Puri's Kumbharpada area alerted police about a foul smell coming from a locked room rented by Gajapati district native Madan Gajanan Dale, 40, and his mother Annapurna, police said.Dalei was arrested in Jamshedpur, where he was working at a shop, Puri superintendent of police Prateek Singh said.The SP said Dalei had been on the run for 57 days, frequently changing his place of stay and rarely using mobile phones.His arrest followed sustained analysis of CCTV footage and inputs from local sources, he added.Explaining the investigation, Singh said police had acted on a complaint from the house owner in Puri.They opened the locked room and dug up Annapurna's body from the kitchen floor, which had been freshly cemented, PTI reported.Police examined CCTV footage from cameras installed at the rented house and in the surrounding area.The footage showed the accused and his mother leaving the house on the morning of August 20 and sitting near the Jagannath Temple, apparently seeking alms.Investigators also found footage showing the accused purchasing sand and cement on August 21, providing important clues during the probe, the SP said.He added that the woman might have been killed on the night of August 20, after which the accused allegedly buried her body in the kitchen.Asked about the motive, the SP said, “Though he has confessed to the crime, he is yet to reveal the reason behind the incident."During the search for Dalei, Puri Police visited his native place, Parlakhemundi, and learnt that he had contacted his sister, who lived in Kolkata. Police subsequently received a clue about his whereabouts in Jamshedpur.By the time police reached the industrial town in Jharkhand, Dalei had fled.Police officials also visited Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu and announced rewards at various places for his capture, Singh said.However, acting on recent information, police arrested Dalei from a snack shop in Jamshedpur, he added.(With agency inputs)Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Delhi BJP leader burns giant cockroach effigy; CJP founder responds with SRK’s 'Swades' song
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations at Netaji Subhash Place in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 30-foot cockroach effigy was burnt alongside those of Ravan, Kumbhkaran and Meghnad during Dussehra celebrations at Netaji Subhash Place in Delhi on Tuesday. The move drew sharp reactions from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders and sparking a debate on social media.While the organisers said the effigy symbolised filth and promoted cleanliness, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a snippet from the film Swades, featuring the lyrics "mann se raavan jo nikaale, ram uske mann mei hai (One who casts Ravana out through contemplation, Ram dwells there)."In a separate post he also thanked them for the "free publicity"."Thank you for the free publicity," Dipke said on X, sharing a post about the effigy.CJP legal head Ratna Singh described the development as "tamasha" as she wrote, "Tamasha kara lo bas is desh mein (Just let this country turn everything into a spectacle.)"In another post, she said the incident showed that the CJP had "done something right"."Burning a cockroach effigy on Dussehra only shows how rattled the ruling party is... Good to know we are making enough of an impact for you to see us as competition," she said."Clearly, we are doing something right. Give your IT cell some time off as well. You must be tired after all this (useless) hard work," Singh added.Why was the cockroach effigy burnt?The 30-foot effigy was burnt at the DDA ground in Netaji Subhash Place, Pitampura, alongside those of Ravan, his brother Kumbhkaran and son Meghnad. The event, organised by the Shri Keshav Ram Leela Committee, drew a large crowd.Committee president Ashok Goel Devaraha, a BJP MLA from Model Town, said the cockroach represented filth and unhygienic surroundings. He said the initiative aimed to raise awareness about related health problems, including allergies and asthma.The committee said the effigy was part of its efforts to promote cleanliness under the Swachh Bharat and Swachh Delhi campaigns. Devaraha said it burns an additional effigy representing a social problem every year, citing previous examples linked to COVID-19, Naxalism and foreign goods.Reacting to an AAP complaint about the effigy, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra said, "The effigy being burnt is that of a cockroach, yet it is the 'termites'—the political termites of this nation—who are feeling the pain."He further added, "The public has its own unique 'pesticide' to deal with them. A cockroach is a symbol of filth and chaos. The people want such effigies to be burnt; just as anti-national forces emerge, their defeat in India is inevitable."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
